scenario.fault_family: link cut (both fabric uplinks of one leaf)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports a total outage: nothing across the
fabric responds, and pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) cannot reach pc_0_1 either.
pc_0_1 CAN still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1, and leaf_router_0_1
itself is up and reachable on its console -- its FRR daemons are all
running. Both of its BGP sessions to the spines are gone. Diagnose.

ip link set eth0 down
  ip link set eth1 down

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 eth0 and eth1 -- BOTH fabric
  uplinks: eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, link subnet 172.16.0.6/31) to
  spine_router_0_0 and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, link subnet
  172.16.0.10/31) to spine_router_0_1
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1's only paths into the CLOS fabric are its
  two spine uplinks. With both interfaces down, both BGP sessions drop
  and the leaf can neither learn 10.0.0.0/24 nor deliver its own
  10.0.1.0/24 traffic anywhere -- the CLOS redundancy is defeated
  because BOTH members of the redundant pair are down. The host-facing
  port eth2 (10.0.1.1/24) is untouched, so pc_0_1 still reaches its
  gateway but nothing beyond it. Note this is the one link-fault shape
  where redundancy does not save the leaf; a single downed uplink
  would only degrade redundancy.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both spine-facing interfaces (eth0, eth1) down on
  leaf_router_0_1
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` and `ip link set eth1 up` on
  leaf_router_0_1; both BGP sessions re-establish on their own.
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1. Once
the uplinks are UP the sessions to both spines come back and pc_0_1
regains fabric reachability.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** Both uplink interfaces of leaf_router_0_1 — eth0 (connecting to spine_router_0_0) and eth1 (connecting to spine_router_0_1) — are in a DOWN state (no IFF_UP, no LOWER_UP carrier flag), while the peer interfaces on both spine routers remain fully UP.

**Mechanism:** With both uplinks down, leaf_router_0_1 cannot form TCP connections to its BGP neighbors at 172.16.0.6 (spine_router_0_0) and 172.16.0.10 (spine_router_0_1). BGP therefore stays in `Active` state — perpetually attempting to connect but never succeeding. Without established BGP sessions, leaf_router_0_1 never receives routes to any prefix beyond its local segment (10.0.1.0/24), and it never advertises 10.0.1.0/24 up the fabric. The result is that pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) can only reach its local gateway (10.0.1.1 on eth2, which is UP), while all cross-fabric traffic — including to pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) — is returned with an ICMP Destination Net Unreachable by the leaf itself.

**Localization:** leaf_router_0_1, interfaces eth0 and eth1. The BGP configuration (ASNs, neighbor IPs, network advertisement) is entirely correct and matches both spine configs.

**Root cause:** Both spine-facing interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 were brought down (link_down or link_detach), severing all L3 connectivity from the leaf to the spine layer and collapsing both BGP sessions to Active state.

**Fix:** Restore the downed interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 — `ip link set eth0 up` and `ip link set eth1 up` (or reattach the virtual interfaces to their bridges if detached). BGP will re-establish automatically within seconds, routes will be exchanged, and full fabric reachability for pc_0_1 will be restored.

The agent's remediation to bring eth0 and eth1 up (or reattach them) on leaf_router_0_1 exactly matches the expected fix and will restore BGP and fabric reachability.
